title: Prefetch Economist: Policy Compiler for KV TTL and Safe Rollback Harness
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a telemetry-driven policy compiler (Prefetch Economist) that generates per-prefix TTL and prefetch recommendations, synthesizes cache key transformations, and emits a safe, staged rollout plan with automated canary/rollback triggers. The compiler will combine econometric hit-rate models, request-level batching signals, and cost impact simulations to suggest conservative defaults and a sequence of incremental applies with guardrails.
background: We have many ad-hoc prefix TTL changes that either underperform (low hit uplift) or cause regressions (latency/cost spikes and unexpected cold misses). Existing playbooks require manual synthesis of sampling results and a lot of heuristics. This ticket creates an automated translator from telemetry -> policy + rollout manifest with embedded safety checks and a compact guide for engineers/PMs to apply changes with minimal risk.
goals: Produce per-prefix TTL suggestions with estimated hit uplift and expected token-cost delta
Output a staged rollout manifest (canary cohorts, shadow replay, metrics to watch, automatic revert criteria)
Provide cache key normalization recommendations to reduce prefix cardinality and collision risk
Integrate with existing canary framework to auto-trigger reverts when thresholds are breached
Reduce median per-token cost for targeted workloads by >= 8% without violating latency SLOs
non_goals: Model training for new ML hit predictors (we will use econometric/GLM and rule-based hybrids first)
Replacing the runtime eviction logic (only policy suggestions and rollout orchestration)
UI work in Console (we will emit artifacts; separate PM ticket will handle Console integration)
approach: Aggregate 14 days of prefix telemetry: request rate, suffix length distribution, observed KV hits, backend tokens saved, latency, and tenant metadata
Fit an econometric hit-rate model per prefix using a regularized Poisson/GLM to predict hit-probabilities as TTL varies
Simulate TTL uplift scenarios to estimate incremental cache hits, expected cost savings, and tail latency impact
Derive a prioritized list of prefixes where net economic benefit exceeds conservative safety margins
Generate a rollout manifest with staggered cohort sizes, shadow replay hooks, metric thresholds, and an automated rollback recipe
Include cache key transformation suggestions (affix trimming, canonicalization rules, suffix bucketing) with collision risk score
Expose CLI to produce artifacts and a dry-run mode that runs the simulation using historical traffic for confidence scoring
success_metrics: Automated suggestions adopted for at least 3 production customers within first 8 weeks
Measurable median per-token cost reduction >= 8% for adopters on targeted workloads
Zero Sev incidents attributable to automated apply when following recommended rollout manifest
At least 90% of suggested rollouts complete without requiring manual full rollback
acceptance_criteria: CLI can produce a policy artifact (.yaml) per input tenant containing per-prefix TTL, prefetch flags, and rollout manifest
Simulator can replay 7 days of historical traffic and produce estimated hit uplift and token-cost delta within a reasonable confidence interval
Rollout manifest contains explicit canary cohorts, metric thresholds, and a machine-actionable revert trigger definition
Proof-of-concept integration with shadow-canary infra that can apply staged changes to 1%/10%/100% cohorts with auto-revert
Documentation and runbook published with example analysis for at least two distinct workload archetypes (low-cardinality sparse prefixes, high-cardinality conversational prefixes)
Security review signoff for telemetry ingestion path and manifest storage
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Hit model mis-specification for sparse prefixes leading to over-aggressive TTLs. Mitigation: Add minimum-sample thresholds and require shadow-replay validation before canary escalation.
Risk: Prefix cardinality explosion after key-normalization changes. Mitigation: Provide collision risk scoring and require manual approval for transformations with score > 0.3.
Risk: Sudden backend load if prefetch is misconfigured. Mitigation: Default prefetch=false and recommend conservative prefetch budgets; include burst-limiter in rollout manifest.
Risk: Telemetry gaps cause poor estimates. Mitigation: Flag prefixes with incomplete telemetry and mark them as 'insufficient data' in recommendations.
implementation_notes: Telemetry ingestion: extend existing prefix-telemetry pipeline to emit per-tenancy prefix histograms and per-request KV lookup outcomes
Model fitting: use statsmodels or scikit-learn GLM with L2 regularization; prefer explainable coefficients for quick audits
Simulator: deterministic replay harness that can apply candidate TTLs and compute synthetic hit traces; keep random seeds fixed for repeatability
Rollout manifest format: yaml with fields (prefix, ttl_seconds, prefetch, cohorts, metrics_to_watch, revert_conditions, owner_contact)
Integration: implement a small shim in canary service that can read manifests and orchestrate staggered applies with automatic revert on threshold breach
Observability: wire dashboards for per-prefix KPIs (hit_rate, backend_req_rate, token_cost, p95_latency) and alerting on revert events
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Dry run: run compiler in dry-run mode on last 14 days for three customers and review artifacts with PM/Eng/DS
Phase 1 - Shadow replay: enable shadow replay for top 50 prefixes by potential savings for one tenant for 48 hours
Phase 2 - Canary apply: apply to 1% cohort for 24h; auto-revert if backend_req_rate increases > 15% or token_cost delta worse than predicted by >10%
Phase 3 - Scale canary: if Phase 2 stable, expand to 10% cohort for 48h; continue monitoring and manual review
Phase 4 - Full apply: gradual ramp to 100% with continued monitoring and scheduled post-mortem in 7 days
progress_updates: 2026-02-26 - Kickoff meeting with DS and runtime team; agreed on GLM baseline and telemetry schema
2026-03-03 - Prototype simulator completed; initial replay on anonymized traffic shows plausible hit uplift for conversational prefixes
2026-03-08 - First draft of rollout manifest schema reviewed by SRE; added automatic revert criteria and burst-limiter
2026-03-11 - Integrated collision-risk heuristic for key-normalization suggestions; added manual approval flag for high-risk transforms
2026-03-12 - Began wiring shadow-canary integration; mock-run scheduled against dev tenant traffic next week
open_questions: What are acceptable default conservative TTLs for low-sample prefixes? Suggested defaults exist but need PM signoff
Who is the final owner for approving cache key normalization changes that may affect downstream analytics?
Do we want an automated email/Slack ping to owners on auto-revert, or rely solely on console alerts?
